title: POST https://api-ar-game.bistudio.com/game-api/api/v2.0/servers/auth (and /servers/auth/refresh)
$comment: Probed directly on 1.8.0.13. This is the OAuth-style exchange for a server: the token from servers/createToken goes into the Authorization header as `ServerToken <value>`, and the answer carries a short-lived serverAccessToken. The auth type had to be found by experiment - the service answers `Authorization: <type> <value>` is the expected format, and refuses Bearer, Basic, Token, JWT, Client, Steam, Server, Owner, S2S, Anonymous, None, ApiKey, ClientSecret, serverToken, ownerToken, gameClientToken, identityToken, accessToken and CommunitySelfHosted with `Invalid auth type '<word>'`; ServerToken is accepted. The access token is an RS256 JWS whose payload is {"iat","exp","id","aid","t"} with exp = iat + expireIn, id = serverId, t = serverType and aid an account id that the anonymous token also gets. servers/auth/refresh wants the same header type and the *server token* again, not the access token: sending the access token answers `InvalidServerToken: Invalid JWT token`, and sending nothing answers `AuthError: Missing server auth.` What a server access token unlocks was not mapped beyond one negative result - userProfiles/getMetadata refuses it as an unsupported token type.

request.description: The request body is empty in the working call; the credential is the header. Headers: `Authorization: ServerToken <serverToken>` together with the x-client-id/x-client-secret pair every call carries.

serverAccessToken.description: The bearer token for this server session. RS256 (the owner/server tokens are RS512), with a `kid` in its header, 1800 s to live in the probe.

serverType.description: 2 = CommunitySelfHosted, echoed from the server token.

serverId.description: Echoed from the server token, and repeated inside the access token's `id` claim.

expireIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires: 1800 in the probe, and exp - iat in the token itself.
